body.statement:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) satisfy \(d_e(G)<\infty\), and suppose a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied for every source-consistent recorded stratum. There is a universal \(a>0\) such that a randomized localized geometric-resolution algorithm returns exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\) with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\). Its arithmetic construction time and certificate length are at most
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),
\]
where \(s=s(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\) and \(\mathfrak d=\mathfrak d(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\). In particular, for any fixed \(b>0\), if \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), then the bound is \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) for a universal \(C\) depending only on \(a\) and \(b\). The output polynomial is the monic minimal polynomial over \(K_G\), not a whole-fiber eliminant, and \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) contains the covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-infinity, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits whose nonzero product is \(h_{G,e}\). The theorem is conditional on the supplied charts; it does not construct or select them.
body.proof_tex:
Fix one source-consistent recorded stratum and invoke \(\mathrm{def:source\mbox{-}prime\mbox{-}chart}\).  Thus \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), \(r\le2k\), \(P=\ker\xi\subset K_G[x]\), and chart validity gives
\[
 PK_G[x]_{H\Delta}
 =(h_1,\ldots,h_c)K_G[x]_{H\Delta},
 \qquad \xi(H\Delta)\ne0,
\tag{36}
\]
where \(c=\operatorname{ht}P\), the localized sequence is reduced and regular, and \(\Delta\) is a nonzero \(c\)-by-\(c\) Jacobian minor.  Therefore (36) presents the localization of the source prime rather than an extraneous residual component.  It is smooth and pure dimensional of dimension
\[
 q=r-c\le2k.
\tag{37}
\]
The principal open set is encoded polynomially by adjoining \(u\) and \(uH\Delta-1=0\).

Put \(E=K_G(\lambda_e)\).  The hypothesis \(d_e(G)<\infty\) and characteristic zero make \(E/K_G\) finite separable.  For every \(K_G\)-embedding \(\tau:E\to\overline{K_G}\), the algebra \(L\otimes_{E,\tau}\overline{K_G}\) is nonzero: choose an \(E\)-transcendence basis of \(L\), after which the remaining extension is algebraic, and use faithful flatness of field extension.  Hence the base-changed source-prime chart has a nonempty component above every conjugate of \(\lambda_e\), with \(H\Delta\) nonzero on it.

Generic affine hyperplanes meet each positive-dimensional component properly.  There are only \(d_e(G)\) conjugate components, so the intersection of their nonempty open sets of admissible choices is nonempty.  Choose \(q\) affine linear forms whose successive intersections are transverse, zero dimensional, and nonempty on every conjugate component.  This is the transverse slicing operation covered by \(\mathrm{lem:groebner\mbox{-}free\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\); randomized choices outside the finitely many determinant and leading-form hypersurfaces have the required property.

Apply that lemma to the localized regular sequence and the \(q\) slices.  On successful choices it returns a finite reduced algebra \(B_{\mathfrak C}\), multiplication matrices, and a primitive-element representation.  The chart's rational lifting circuits recover every eliminated directed coordinate, including \(\lambda_e\), and their validity identities make every original residual vanish in the source-prime localization.  Let \(M_{e,\mathfrak C}\) denote multiplication by the recovered \(\lambda_e\), and put
\[
 \chi_{e,\mathfrak C}(t)=\det(tI-M_{e,\mathfrak C}).
\tag{38}
\]
Every root recorded by (38) is a conjugate of \(\lambda_e\).  Conversely, the common slices meet every conjugate component, so every conjugate occurs for at least one chart.  It follows that
\[
 p_e(t)=\operatorname{sqfree}\!\left(
   \prod_{\mathfrak C}\chi_{e,\mathfrak C}(t)
 \right),
 \qquad \deg p_e=d_e(G).
\tag{39}
\]
Indeed, the right side is the unique monic polynomial whose roots are exactly the distinct \(K_G\)-conjugates of \(\lambda_e\).  This proves a single-coordinate claim even when the unsliced fiber is positive dimensional.

All chart coefficients and lifting maps are rational arithmetic circuits in covariance entries.  Determinants, multiplication-matrix operations, differentiation, subresultant greatest-common-divisor computation, squarefree extraction, and monic normalization are arithmetic-circuit operations over \(K_G\), so (39) gives rational circuits for every coefficient of \(p_e\).  For each lifting identity, clearing covariance denominators records its denominators and the resulting original-incidence identity.  Homogenization before slicing records projective leading forms; univariate normalization records the specialized leading coefficient and squarefreeness resultant.  Covariance-localization factors are retained separately, and real sign data are checked after substitution into the original residuals.  These finitely many nonzero circuits form \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), and their repetition-free cleared product is \(h_{G,e}\).  Equation (36) and \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) ensure that no directed-coordinate expression is inverted, so every pole or identically zero-over-zero stratum is represented by a supplied valid chart or retained by an original-incidence check.

For arbitrary recorded equations and inequations use \(\mathrm{lem:lifting\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}equidimensional\mbox{-}decomposition}\); for regular localized slices use \(\mathrm{lem:groebner\mbox{-}free\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\).  Their complexity bounds, (37), multiplication-matrix linear algebra, and exact sign determination on the returned univariate representations give a universal \(a>0\) such that total arithmetic work and output length are at most
\[
 (n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a
 \operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),
\tag{40}
\]
where \(s=s(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\) and \(\mathfrak d=\mathfrak d(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\).  The latter parameter includes all successive intersections, localizations, slices, and lifting fibers, so (40) charges every created branch.

Every randomized decision is a nonvanishing test for an explicit chart, transversality, leading-form, lifting, or resultant polynomial.  If their degree bounds are \(d_1,\ldots,d_M\), sample independently from finite sets \(S_j\) with \(d_j/|S_j|\le\delta/M\).  The Schwartz--Zippel lemma and a union bound give
\[
 \Pr(\text{some symbolic genericity decision is wrong})
 \le\sum_{j=1}^M\frac{d_j}{|S_j|}\le\delta.
\tag{41}
\]
On the complementary event, (36)--(39) prove that the returned tuple is exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\).

Finally, if \(s\le n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\le n^{b(k+1)}\), then for \(n\ge2\), after enlarging a constant,
\[
 (n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a
 \le n^{a(\max\{1,b\}+1+b)(k+1)}
 \le n^{C(k+1)}.
\tag{42}
\]
This proves the fixed-parameter specialization.  The construction starts from a supplied valid localized source-prime chart and does not claim to select that embedded prime or construct its source-nonzero Jacobian minor.
body.justification: A valid localized reduced source-prime chart is sufficient for exact coordinate minimal-polynomial and specialization-certificate construction.
body.gap: Giusti--Lecerf--Salvy and Lecerf do not select or descend the embedded SEM source prime, and their complexity retains geometric-degree dependence.
body.consumer: This is the exact higher-degree polynomial-output contract for a chart-certified extension of fasttreeid.
